Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: 
The test case fails on this assertion: `assertFalse(sb.contains('h'))` after deleting the substring "three" from "onetwothree". The expected result is that the character 'h' should not be found after deletion, because "three" contains the 'h' characters.

Looking at the implementation of `StrBuilder.contains(char)`, the method loops over `thisBuf.length`, where `thisBuf` points to the underlying `buffer` char array. This is problematic because the buffer can be longer than the logical size of the string stored in StrBuilder, as indicated by the separate `size` field. The `buffer` array length indicates the capacity of the internal char array, not the actual number of characters currently in the StrBuilder.

This discrepancy leads to the `contains(char)` method searching beyond the valid content (up to the field `size`), potentially returning `true` for characters that are not actually in the logical string stored in the builder but remain in the unused buffer space.

The bug report summary also confirms this: "StrBuilder contains usages of thisBuf.length when they should use size" indicates that in several places including `contains(char)`, the code uses `buffer.length` (i.e., `thisBuf.length`) instead of the logical `size` of the string.

The test case fails because after deleting "three", the `buffer` still contains old characters beyond the new size but `contains` examines the whole buffer length, which makes it erroneously find 'h' that should no longer be considered part of the content.

Other methods such as `indexOf(String, int)`, `deleteFirst(String)`, and `deleteImpl(...)` properly respect the `size` field, supporting the conclusion that the issue lies specifically with `contains(char)` method using `thisBuf.length` instead of `size`.

In summary, the root cause is that `StrBuilder.contains(char)` uses `buffer.length` in the loop boundary instead of `size`, causing it to check characters beyond the logical end of the string buffer and leading to incorrect behavior in the test case.

The fix is to change the loop in `contains(char)` to iterate up to `size` instead of `buffer.length`.

---

Suggested methods to fix:
- org.apache.commons.lang.text.StrBuilder.contains(char)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
